title: Akshay Kumar Just Dropped a Song Called 'Deewane Hain' and the Entire Welcome Franchise Came to the Party.
excerpt: Nineteen years after he first walked into the chaos, Akshay Kumar reunites with director Ahmed Khan for Welcome To The Jungle — and the new 'Deewane Hain' teaser promises the loudest, most overstuffed Bollywood blowout of the summer, in cinemas June 26.
body:
The teaser dropped on a Wednesday morning and within hours the internet was doing the thing it always does when Akshay Kumar decides to be silly again — surrendering completely. 'Deewane Hain', the first song teaser from Welcome To The Jungle, landed on June 17 with a single promise scrawled across the screen: jungle ke jashn mein ab saare deewane hain. Translation — everyone's lost their minds, and you're invited. The full track arrives tomorrow. The film arrives June 26. And if the teaser is anything to go by, restraint was not on the call sheet.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=3CDOd4GdcUQ

This is the third instalment in the Welcome franchise, the slapstick empire Firoz A. Nadiadwala built on the back of Anees Bazmee's 2007 original and its 2015 sequel. What makes this one feel like an event isn't just the comedy — it's the reunion. Akshay Kumar is back with director Ahmed Khan for the first time in nineteen years, and the nostalgia is doing real work here.

"There's a lot of nostalgia attached to the Welcome franchise." — Akshay Kumar, on reuniting with Ahmed Khan after 19 years

Khan, for his part, has been teasing something stranger than pure farce. "Watch it on mute and it looks serious," he said of the film — a cheeky promise that beneath the gadhe-aur-ghode chaos there's an actual movie trying to get made. The conceit, revealed in the May teaser, is gloriously meta: a fake film that has gone catastrophically wrong, with Akshay's character storming off set mid-shoot before being lured back by the only thing that matters — the paycheck. The teaser even opened with a disclaimer for the ages: "In the making of this film, no animals were used. Sivaay kuchh ghodon ke aur hum gadhon ke" — except for a few horses, and donkeys like us.

Then there's the cast, which reads less like a call sheet and more like a wedding guest list someone forgot to trim. Suniel Shetty, Paresh Rawal, Sanjay Dutt, Arshad Warsi, Jackie Shroff, Raveena Tandon, Lara Dutta, Jacqueline Fernandez, Disha Patani, Tusshar Kapoor, Johny Lever, Rajpal Yadav, Krushna Abhishek, Kiku Sharda — and that's the abbreviated version. It is one of the largest ensembles assembled for a Hindi film in recent memory, and 'Deewane Hain' looks like the number where every last one of them gets to shimmy through frame.

The music is its own statement of intent. The franchise's sonic DNA — those original Sajid-Wajid compositions — has been recreated by Vikram Montrose, with the title track already out featuring vocals from Shaan, Priya Patidar and Montrose himself. The full soundtrack runs to six tracks: groove anthems, glamorous dance numbers, grand cinematic set pieces. "We wanted every song to feel cinematic, entertaining, and mounted on a massive scale," Khan said. Nobody is making Welcome To The Jungle for the arthouse crowd, and that is precisely the point.

For Akshay, the timing is delicious. He's riding the wave of Bhooth Bangla, Priyadarshan's ₹264-crore horror-comedy that recently landed on Netflix, and Welcome To The Jungle gives him a second swing at the broad, theatre-packing comedy lane he practically built. After a couple of lean years, Khiladi Kumar in full slapstick mode is a comfort-food proposition the box office has historically rewarded.

For the diaspora, the logistics are clean. JioStar has acquired the film's theatrical, satellite and OTT rights, which means a worldwide cinema release on June 26 followed eventually by a digital home on JioHotstar — the same pipeline that's served NRIs well for the studio's recent slate. For families across the US, UK, Canada and Australia, this is shaping up as the multi-generational summer outing: loud enough for the kids, nostalgic enough for the parents who remember the first Welcome on a worn-out DVD.

Is it going to be high art? Absolutely not. Is it going to be the most crowded, most chaotic, most unapologetically Bollywood thing in theatres this month? The teaser is daring you to bet against it. 'Deewane Hain' drops in full tomorrow — clear some space on your timeline, because the jungle is about to get very, very loud.
